expectations.text: Identifies heat emission / plant heads or fruits cooling below dew point as the cause of free water, not just high RH
expectations.evidence: Explains heat emission to the cold roof/sky and cold air drop cooling heads and lagging fruits below dew point; says RH 90% is not the real problem

expectations.text: Recommends closing the screen fully (no moisture gap) or a double screen, explaining that gaps drop cold air and create cold spots
expectations.evidence: Step 2: go from 95% to fully closed; explains gap circulation up to ~8 C and cold spots

expectations.text: Recommends removing moisture by condensation on the roof and/or ventilating above the closed screen instead of gapping
expectations.evidence: Moisture leaves by condensation on the roof and by opening vents a little above the closed screen

expectations.text: Recommends replacing or lowering the minimum pipe temperature and using fans (preferably vertical) for air movement
expectations.evidence: Replace fixed minimum pipe with demand-driven heating; use vertical fans instead of pipe heat

expectations.text: Addresses morning condensation on fruits: raise temperature gradually before sunrise and/or keep the screen closed until the air above it has warmed
expectations.evidence: Raise temperature gradually well before sunrise; keep screen closed until air above it has warmed

expectations.text: Recommends monitoring absolute humidity / dew point versus crop temperature (e.g. aspirator box above the screen, leaf or fruit temperature)
expectations.evidence: AH at three points, aspirator box above the screen, IR head temperature vs dew point, fruit temperature at sunrise

expectations.text: Warns that shading/whitewash cuts photosynthesis and can start a negative spiral, and advises trying humidity and water-supply measures first
expectations.evidence: Section 'Why shading is the wrong first step' describes the shading spiral; fix ventilation and watering first

expectations.text: Recommends ventilating less / allowing a higher temperature (e.g. 26-28 C) to keep humidity and CO2 inside on sunny days
expectations.evidence: Raise vent temperature, cites 28 vs 25 C / 75% RH example, ventilate less

expectations.text: Explains that evaporation is driven by absorbed energy (radiation) rather than by low RH, and that warm leaves indicate closing stomata / water stress
expectations.evidence: 'a plant evaporates roughly in proportion to the radiation it absorbs, whatever the air humidity'; warm leaves = stomata closing

expectations.text: Recommends measuring leaf temperature and/or VPD, with roughly 0.3-1.5 kPa as healthy and above ~1.5 kPa as stress
expectations.evidence: IR leaf temperature vs air; VPD from leaf temp, healthy 0.3-1.5 kPa, stress from ~1.5 kPa

expectations.text: Addresses water supply or root uptake (e.g. irrigation based on radiation, ramping up in the morning, root health)
expectations.evidence: Irrigate on accumulated radiation, ramp from sunrise, check roots/root temperature, fruit buffer

expectations.text: Mentions misting or another way to raise RH under high radiation, and/or the CO2 lost through wide-open vents
expectations.evidence: Misting controlled on radiation/PAR/leaf temp; CO2 blown out by wide vents

expectations.text: Defines RTR as the ratio of 24-hour average temperature to the daily light (radiation/PAR) sum
expectations.evidence: RTR links 24-hour average temperature to daily light sum

expectations.text: Describes plotting each day as a point (light sum vs average temperature) and following a target line
expectations.evidence: Scatterplot one dot per day, fit trend line, target line with band

expectations.text: Explains the too-strong/vegetative (more light, same temperature) vs too-weak/generative (higher temperature, little light) logic
expectations.evidence: Table: more light same temp = too strong/vegetative; higher temp no light = weak/generative

expectations.text: Gives the day-to-day practice: after a sunny day keep the night warmer or postpone the drop, after a dark day keep the night cooler
expectations.evidence: After a sunny day postpone drop and keep night warmer; after a dark day keep night cooler

expectations.text: Links RTR to plant load planned against the expected (long-term average) light curve, noting a lower load allows a higher temperature per unit light
expectations.evidence: Plant load vs 10-year weekly light curve; lower load allows raising the RTR line

expectations.text: Notes preconditions or corrections: CO2/RH not limiting, and PAR at crop level is better than outdoor radiation when whitewash/screens cut light
